alignments.note: In the καὶ … δέ idiom δέ is the sentence connective and καί is the adjunctive particle emphasizing πάντες, so the ASV's emphatic Yea is what answers to καί and the plain connective and to δέ. The competing reading, which the earlier pass took, gives and to καί as its ordinary gloss and Yea to δέ; it is defensible, but it crosses the two tokens for no gain, and rule 100 counts a crossed alignment against a reading where an uncrossed one is equally available.
Quantifier rendered all. Rule 80's whosoever compression is not in question: the ASV writes a separate English word beside the quantifier, so the ordinary split applies.
Connective δέ realized by and, the word carrying the coordination in the English clause; see s001 for the competing assignment of Yea and and across the two particles.

Substantival article before a participle with a single relativizer written for the pair; rule 90 gives that to the article, a single relativizer being pronoun and relativizer at once. Rule 80's every one that hath shape is the contrast and does not apply, no separate antecedent pronoun being written; rule 31 does not apply either, no head noun being expressed.
Participle of willing rendered by the modal would, which realizes θέλω's own volitional sense rather than serving as an auxiliary of the following infinitive; the infinitive keeps live under rule 2.
Infinitive rendered live. SBLGNT.2TI.3.12.v003 is underdetermined over s006–s007 and the projection's base reading is compatible with the English, so rule 12 leaves it alone.
Name, split from Jesus under rule 26.

One passive verb rendered by the support phrase shall suffer persecution; the future auxiliary rides inside the unit under rule 9. Rule 91's test puts the head on persecution, the word the corpus spends on διώκω, suffer being the empty support verb exactly as bear witness heads on witness.

review_notes: Only the two opening particles changed: καί now takes Yea and δέ takes and, reversing the accepted pass. The reasoning is functional rather than positional — δέ is the connective in the καὶ … δέ idiom and English and is the connective in Yea, and all …, while adjunctive καί is what the emphatic Yea answers to. The swap also removes a crossing the accepted reading had no need of.

Both particle assignments remain defensible and rule 16 required a note naming the competing one; the accepted unit notes gave none, which is the main reason this verse is returned corrected rather than unchanged.

A later reader may want to check LUK.2.35 for consistency: it carries the same καὶ … δέ construction rendered yea and, and that chapter is already finalized in this corpus. I could not query it from this briefing, so this verse was decided on the contract alone. If LUK.2.35 assigns the pair the other way, rule 24's habit argues for making the two match rather than following the surface of either verse.
All other units stand as accepted, including the rule 90 reading of οἱ → that against giving the relativizer to the participle, and the rule 91 head on persecution.
